# gitmoap_repository_pipelines (Data Source)

List a repository's pipeline definitions. Published pipelines by default; `?status=draft|published|all` chooses. Drafts are listed only to those who can write pipelines (Maintainer and above).

The token needs `pipeline:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository id

### Optional

- `status` (String) Lifecycle filter: draft | published | all (default published; drafts writers-only)

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `component_instances` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--component_instances))
- `created_at` (String) RFC 3339.
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--created_by))
- `description` (String)
- `diagnostics` (Attributes) The result of validating a pipeline definition: reported on a draft, and returned with a `400`
when saving a published definition fails. Each problem carries a stable `code`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--diagnostics))
- `edges` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--edges))
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `repo_id` (String)
- `source` (Attributes) Where on the default branch a pipeline is declared. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--source))
- `stages` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--stages))
- `status` (String) Whether a pipeline definition can run. A `draft` is saved even when it is invalid — problems are
reported, not refused — and cannot be run; a `published` definition must be valid to be saved,
and can be run.
- `updated_at` (String) RFC 3339.

<a id="nestedatt--items--component_instances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.component_instances`

Read-Only:

- `component_id` (String)
- `component_ref` (String) The reference as the author wrote it, kept for display. It is not used to find the
component.
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String) Display name, also put in front of the display names of the steps it expands into.
- `stage_map` (Map of String) Maps every stage slot the component declares to a stage of this pipeline, keeping the slots'
order.
- `version` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.


<a id="nestedatt--items--diagnostics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.diagnostics`

Read-Only:

- `valid` (Boolean)
- `violations` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--diagnostics--violations))
- `warnings` (Attributes List) Things worth knowing that do not make the definition invalid, such as a deprecated
component version. A violation stops a published definition from being saved; a warning
never does. Left out when there are none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--diagnostics--warnings))

<a id="nestedatt--items--diagnostics--violations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.diagnostics.violations`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) Stable machine-readable code (e.g. `cycle_detected`, `type_mismatch`,
`required_input_not_wired`).
- `message` (String) Human-readable description.
- `target` (Attributes) The part of the pipeline a validation problem points at. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--diagnostics--violations--target))

<a id="nestedatt--items--diagnostics--violations--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.diagnostics.violations.target`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Id of the stage, step, connection or component instance at fault; empty for a problem with
the pipeline as a whole.
- `kind` (String) Which kind of element a validation violation targets.



<a id="nestedatt--items--diagnostics--warnings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.diagnostics.warnings`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) Stable machine code — the warning rule's own name, exactly as a violation's is.
- `message` (String)
- `warnings_target` (Attributes) The part of the pipeline a validation problem points at. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--diagnostics--warnings--warnings_target))

<a id="nestedatt--items--diagnostics--warnings--warnings_target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.diagnostics.warnings.warnings_target`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Id of the stage, step, connection or component instance at fault; empty for a problem with
the pipeline as a whole.
- `kind` (String) Which kind of element a validation violation targets.




<a id="nestedatt--items--edges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.edges`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `source_node_id` (String)
- `source_port` (String)
- `target_node_id` (String)
- `target_port` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.source`

Read-Only:

- `commit_sha` (String) The default-branch commit whose change last put the pipeline's content into effect. Absent
for a pipeline its files took over before the commit was recorded.
- `directory` (String) The directory under `.gitmoap/pipelines/` whose files declare it. Absent for a pipeline
last applied before directories were recorded.
- `removed_at` (String) When the pipeline's declaration was removed from the default branch, RFC 3339. The
pipeline keeps its id and its runs and starts nothing until a file declares it again.
Absent while it is declared.
- `stem` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--stages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.stages`

Read-Only:

- `barrier_mode` (String) When a stage is allowed to start. `strict` waits for every step in every earlier stage to finish, so a failure anywhere stops what follows. `lenient` waits only for the steps a given step actually depends on, so an unrelated branch failing does not block it. `strict` is the default.
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `nodes` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--stages--nodes))
- `stage_type` (String) The pipeline stage a capability belongs to. Maps verbatim to the
`stage_type` field of a capability in `gitmoap-provider.yaml`.

<a id="nestedatt--items--stages--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.stages.nodes`

Read-Only:

- `allow_failure` (Boolean) When `true`, this node's failure (a non-zero exit or a timeout, after any
retries) is non-blocking: it does not fail the enclosing stage or the run.
The node's transitive dependents — which can never receive its output —
are skipped, while independent branches and later stages keep running. A
run whose only failures were `allow_failure` nodes finishes
`succeeded_with_warnings`.
- `approval` (Attributes) An approval gate on a step. With no `approvers`, anyone with Developer access to the repository
may decide; a list narrows the decision to the people, teams and roles it names, as they stand
when the approval is given. On a step that deploys to an environment requiring approval, the
list may only name approvers the environment also names. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--stages--nodes--approval))
- `capability_id` (String)
- `changes` (List of String) Path globs that decide whether this step runs: when none of them matches a path the push
changed, the step is skipped. When absent and `service` is set, the service's own path globs
apply.
- `connection` (String)
- `cpu` (String)
- `environment` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `max_retries` (Number)
- `memory` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `resource_group` (Attributes) A resource group a step holds while it runs, so only one step naming it runs at a time. Unless
`mode` says otherwise, a step queues for the group, for as long as the pipeline's timeout
allows unless `max_wait_seconds` sets a shorter limit. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--stages--nodes--resource_group))
- `retry_delay_seconds` (Number)
- `service` (String)
- `timeout_seconds` (Number)
- `variables_from` (String)
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--stages--nodes--approval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.stages.nodes.approval`

Read-Only:

- `required` (Number) Distinct approvals needed, 1–10. On a gated environment the larger of this and the
environment's own count applies.


<a id="nestedatt--items--stages--nodes--resource_group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.stages.nodes.resource_group`

Read-Only:

- `max_wait_seconds` (Number)
- `mode` (String) What happens when a run wants to deploy while another run holds the lock: `queue` (the
default) waits its turn, `skip` skips the step, and `cancel_previous` cancels the other run.
`cancel_previous` is available on environments only, not on a step's resource group.
- `name` (String)
